Section 1: 'comments made by participants in my study'
Section 3: 'Designers who gain skill in the use of a medium or whom are comfortable with its use are able to deal more effectively with place concepts.'
Section 4: 'Those interviewed stated that they work with any and all media'

Section 5: 'For this comparison, insights from literature are complemented with in-depth interviews with people who are congenitally blind.' (p. 103, though this is from a different paper, the current paper refers to 'my doctoral study' and 'respondents' consistently, indicating an interview-based approach)

title: Drawing out Experience; Between Media & Place
authors: Vincent Canizaro, University of Texas at San Antonio

findings.antecedent: Remembered place experiences (touchstone memories, everyday experiences)
findings.consequent: Inspiration for place-based design, designer's ability to judge and conceptualize imagined/designed places, empathetic connectivity to place concepts
findings.quote: the key to understanding places is our past place experiences;” “memorable imagery is basic to architectural design;” and “experiences are key to one’s ability to make places.”

findings.antecedent: Designer's purposeful and implicit intention to be concerned with place concepts
findings.consequent: Effect on the course and outcome of the design process, ability to develop place-based design, design as something to be inhabited not only looked at
findings.quote: place intentions are good because as architects we have to intend a kind of place. The intend part is important for us as designers.

findings.antecedent: Designer's degree of skill and comfort with the use of any design medium
findings.consequent: Effectiveness in dealing with place concepts in design, ability to draw out ideas, gaining a sense of inhabitation
findings.quote: The more skilled and comfortable I am with a tool... the more engaged I am capable of being in the game.

findings.antecedent: Use of multiple forms of media and mixing different media (e.g., plans, sections, elevations, collage)
findings.consequent: More multivalent sense of an emerging design, effective dealing with the multi-faceted phenomenon of place, enhanced understanding of place quality
findings.quote: Drawing place requires many different types of media”; “Through a broad drawing process, by using a lot of different media is how I come to know the quality of the place.

findings.antecedent: Mixed-media practice (combining different media forms like 2D/3D drawings, physical models, digital files)
findings.consequent: Learning a sense of construction, deep connection to surrogate 'site', affected conceptualization of design as a place
findings.quote: They reported learning a sense of construction that accompanies design-build, and more importantly reported feeling a deep connection to their surrogate “site” that affected their conceptualization of the design as a place.

findings.antecedent: Inclusion of text (verbal/written) and physical presence ('non-drawings') as design media
findings.consequent: Increased access for designers to place concepts, creation of new media (e.g., storyboards, pattern language), enhanced sense of inhabitation
findings.quote: When the respondents were queried as to what helped them get a clearer idea of their place, most replied the difference could be accounted by the use of text and the ability to have physical presence on site as the “media.”

findings.antecedent: Adaptation, augmentation, and innovative use of any design medium
findings.consequent: More engaging media, conducive to design in terms of place, enhanced conceptualization of place, empathetic insideness
findings.quote: Phrases such as “feeling through the media,” “living in the drawing,” going “into the spaces in my drawings,” and “being able to understand the building as if I were there, and “running simulations in my mind about the place, about how it would be used” are all examples of what these strategies were aimed at achieving.

findings.antecedent: Inclusion of the human figure in architectural media (as indicators of dimension/depth, empathetic 'ambassador')
findings.consequent: Aid in getting a sense of inhabitation, more complete sense of possible lived inhabitation
findings.source: 5a. The Human Figure as Guide: Motion and Inhabitation
findings.quote: For those surveyed the human figure acts as a sort of empathetic “ambassador” who participates in the space of the drawing or model for the designer.

findings.antecedent: Utilization of familiar or recognizable phenomena (e.g., furniture, artwork) in design media
findings.consequent: Communication of a sense of scale, allowing designer to insert themselves into the depicted environment
findings.quote: The depictions of objects, such as a familiar piece of furniture or artwork can act in a similar fashion to figures by both communicating a sense of scale and allowing the designer to insert themselves into the depicted environment.

findings.antecedent: Realistic depiction and inclusion of phenomenally rich materials and objects in design media
findings.consequent: Sense of immersion, designer more free to deal with the represented thing, empathetic insideness (through transparency)
findings.quote: Realistic depiction also accomplished a sense of immersion within the designed place... empathetic insideness is achieved through transparency.

findings.antecedent: Design media and styles of mediation that are openly structured and foster ambiguity
findings.consequent: Greater idea exploration, more effective dealing with place concepts, allowing for exploration and presenting place concepts in incompleteness
findings.quote: The situation that is conducive to place-making is freedom to draw a lot, and to use a lot of trace,

findings.consequent: Not directly represented by design media
findings.quote: The phenomenon of place is not directly represented by design media, it is therefore dealt with indirectly in architectural design.

findings.consequent: Ambiguous in favoring the conceptualization of place
findings.quote: Design media, despite the individual differences in effectiveness, are as a whole ambiguous in favoring the conceptualization of place.

findings.antecedent: Gaining a sense of inhabitation of the emerging work
findings.consequent: Relationship between media and place defined by empathetic insideness
findings.quote: Key to the conceptualization of place in architectural design is gaining a sense of inhabitation of the emerging work. Thus, the relationship between media and place is defined by empathetic insideness.

limitations: The main limits of the present study are due to its exploratory character and time limitation.

The budget and the duration of the study on intimacy (one year) only made possible punctual meetings with residents, the lack of feedback from residents resulted in the need and the danger of the subjective interpretation of the data abuse.

The language of usages and the evolving way of thinking about the project is still unusual. Therefore there is a need for an interdisciplinary work over the vocabulary to make it understandable and useful for architects.
minimum_safe_summary: This paper, based on a doctoral study involving interviews with participants, identifies six factors crucial for conceptualizing 'place' in architectural design: memorable reference, intending place, skill and comfort with media, multiple and mixed media approaches, innovation and empathy in media use, and freedom and ambiguity in representation. These factors collectively enhance a designer's ability to engage with space in an embodied and empathetic way, moving beyond purely visual representations. The study concludes that the relationship between design media and place is indirect and variable, emphasizing the importance of gaining a sense of inhabitation through 'empathetic insideness'. Limitations include the exploratory nature, time constraints, and the need for interdisciplinary vocabulary development.

mechanism_chain.description: Remembered place experiences, encompassing both significant 'touchstone memories' and routine 'everyday experiences,' are internally processed by designers. This processing involves recall, reflection, and synthesis, which then causally influences various aspects of their design practice, including creative inspiration, cognitive judgment, and empathetic connection to place concepts.
